en: The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain to help it hunt insects in the dark.
Abaca plants, native to the Philippines, are harvested for their strong leaf fibers which are used to make ropes and paper.
The Mindoro tamaraw is a dwarf buffalo endemic to the island of Mindoro and is critically endangered due to habitat loss.
The Philippines sits within the Coral Triangle, which contains the highest diversity of coral reef fish and hard coral species in the world.
The Aedes aegypti mosquito, which spreads dengue fever in the Philippines, breeds in small containers of stagnant water around houses.
The Philippine eagle primarily hunts colugos and small mammals in the forest canopy using its sharp talons and strong beak.
The waling-waling orchid grows high on tree branches in Mindanao forests, adapting to its environment by absorbing moisture from humid air.
The native Philippine mudfish can survive dry seasons by burying itself in mud and breathing atmospheric air through a specialized organ.
Mangrove forests in Philippine coastal areas like Palawan have specialized stilt roots that protect shorelines from erosion and provide fish nurseries.
The water buffalo, or carabao, has very little body hair and wallows in mud to cool its body down during hot Philippine summers.
The Philippine king fern produces millions of tiny spores on the undersides of its massive fronds to reproduce without using seeds.
Eating local yellow and orange fruits like mangoes and papayas provides Filipino children with vitamin A for healthy vision and immunity.
